ch30-open.title: Advanced interface
ch30-open.standfirst: Power-user touches: pop a shared screen into its own window for a second monitor, the floating presenter, and the navigation widget.

ch10-popout.heading: Pop the share into its own window
ch10-popout.lead: The ⧉ button — tooltip "Open in a separate window to drag to another screen" — lifts the live screen out of the in-app viewer and into a standalone, always-on-top window you can drag onto a second monitor. The drawing canvas keeps the rest of your first screen to yourself.
ch10-popout.body: While popped out, the in-app viewer shows the note "Watching in a separate window" in place of the picture, and live captions travel with the share into the pop-out window. Closing the pop-out window — or clicking back in the app — returns the picture to the in-app viewer and brings the captions home. The viewer also re-homes itself automatically if the presenter stops while you're popped out.

note.html: Pop out uses the browser's Document Picture-in-Picture feature, which today is Chromium-only (Chrome, Edge, and similar). On Firefox and Safari the ⧉ button simply doesn't appear, and the in-app viewer remains your way to watch.

diagram.label: In-app viewer → pop-out window on monitor 2
diagram.cap: Pop out moves the live video into its own OS window without re-loading the feed, so the picture never flickers as it leaves the app.

c30-power.heading: Second monitors, floating windows and quick moves
c30-power.lead: A few touches make Canvas M feel roomier. Pop-out a shared screen into its own window and drag it to a second monitor while you keep drawing on the canvas. Keep a speaker in the floating presenter window so you never lose a face. Use the navigation widget (bottom-right) to zoom, reset and open the mini-map.
c30-power.body: These are all optional — the meeting works without them — but on a big screen or a two-monitor desk they turn the room into a proper workspace.
